extracted.intended_audience: European Commission officials, EU policy-makers and interoperability assessors preparing or managing EU initiatives and legislation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing, assessing and managing EU legislation and policies so they are targeted, effective, easy to comply with and impose the least possible burden. Includes evaluation/monitoring, impact assessment, stakeholder consultation and tools to support implementation and digital-ready policy-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Better regulation objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Better regulation’ is about creating legislation that achieves its objectives while being targeted, effective, easy to comply with and with the least burden possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this overarching objective when preparing new initiatives, proposals or when managing existing policies and legislation; use it as the primary yardstick for designing regulatory intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive evaluations and fitness checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive evaluations and fitness checks involve thorough analysis of how existing legislation and spending programmes have been performing, to check that they are efficient, effective, relevant and coherent, and that EU-level intervention is actually adding value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use evaluations/fitness checks to assess past performance and the continued need for intervention; explicitly test efficiency, effectiveness, relevance, coherence and added value of EU-level action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact assessment components
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact assessments look at the problems to be tackled, the objectives to be achieved, the trade-offs to consider, options for action and their potential impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conducting impact assessments, systematically define the problem, set clear objectives, identify and compare policy options, analyse trade-offs and appraise potential impacts (economic, social, environmental, administrative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder consultation and input
rubrics_metrics.description: Input from stakeholders supports this work throughout the policy cycle, to provide policymakers with the best possible evidence base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate stakeholder consultation early and throughout the policy cycle to gather evidence, test options and improve legitimacy and practicability; see Chapter 2 for detailed insights on stakeholder consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance promotion for Member States
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance promotion tools help Member States transpose, implement and apply EU law in a timely and correct manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and deploy tools and supports that facilitate correct and timely transposition and implementation at Member State level; consider administrative capacity and barriers to compliance when drafting measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalisation via the Better Regulation Toolbox
rubrics_metrics.description: The ‘better regulation’ toolbox operationalizes the concepts explained in the guidelines with 69 tools ranging from planning and validating policy initiatives to digital-ready policy-making and cost-benefit analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the toolbox for practical, operational guidance on specific aspects (e.g., planning/validation of initiatives, making policy digital-ready, conducting cost-benefit analysis); consult both the guidelines and toolbox together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to interoperability assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: These guidelines can also offer valuable insights on different processes that are also relevant for the performance of interoperability assessments under the Interoperable Europe Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the guidance on stakeholder consultation (Chapter 2) and on evaluation and monitoring (Chapters 3 and 4) when conducting interoperability assessments to ensure evidence-based, coherent and implementable interoperability solutions.
